picks.title: AI beats scientists at finding errors in clinical research papers
picks.rationale: Top-tier outlet; AI outperforms human reviewers at catching technical flaws in clinical studies that drive medical decisions — direct patient-safety and evidence-quality angle.
picks.excerpt: New findings demonstrate AI's aptitude for identifying technical flaws in clinical studies where medical decisions are on the line, outperforming human scientists. (Page Cloudflare-gated; date from Crossref created, image from RSS enclosure.)

picks.title: AI-interpreted echocardiograms comparable to human reports, cardiologists' time cut by about 50%
picks.rationale: AHA 2026 study: AI-assisted echo reads match standard reports and halve cardiologist reading time — a concrete clinical workflow result, distinct from the 11-06 rural-scan and 11-09 PARAMOUNT AHA items.
picks.excerpt: AHA Scientific Sessions 2026: in a study testing an AI model for evaluating echocardiograms, AI-assisted interpretation was comparable to standard human reports and cut cardiologists' reading time by about half.

picks.title: LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts future PTSD risk from emergency department trauma narratives with expert-level accuracy
picks.rationale: Open-source LLM ensemble flags one-month PTSD risk from a single routine ED question, catching all 30 cases vs 89% for a PTSD specialist — new mental-health screening tool at the point of care.
picks.excerpt: NYU Langone's open-source LLM ensemble PREVIA predicts one-month PTSD risk from ED patients' answer to a single routine-care question ('What brought you to the ED?'); on 30 patients who developed PTSD it flagged all, versus 89% for a PTSD-specialist clinician.

picks.title: How early efforts to build autonomous clinical AI tools are approaching regulation
picks.rationale: Regulator-facing: teams in ARPA-H's ADVOCATE autonomous clinical-agent program are already meeting FDA within two months of launch — first look at how autonomous clinical AI enters the approval pathway.
picks.excerpt: Multiple teams in ARPA-H's ADVOCATE program, which funds autonomous clinical AI agents, have already held initial informational meetings with the FDA less than two months after the program launched. (Registration wall; body partial.)

picks.title: Hospitals write off $132B as AI fails to move the needle with finances
picks.rationale: New analysis: despite billions spent on AI and automation for revenue-cycle and claims work, hospital bad debt and write-offs keep rising — a reality check on AI in hospital operations.
picks.excerpt: Hospitals are losing more money from bad debt and write-offs despite investing billions into automation and AI to improve revenue-cycle performance, a new analysis finds.

dedup.note: Pool 14, no story_dedup drops. Dropped: Doximity 190 health systems (history_match related to 10-26 Doximity/UpToDate; customer-count update, no new release -> running story, also business). Dropped as non-qualifying: Siggy launch (pre-seed funding), STAT heart-drug-failures (opinion/analysis), MedCity 'challenge after approval' (opinion), STAT men/chatbots (feature, weaker than picks). Not picked on ranking/diversity: Lunit-Saudi and USARad-AZmed (AuntMinnie deployment deals; imaging already covered by AHA echo), NEJM AI AURA RCT (no og_image, thin abstract), MambaSleepCVD (no og_image). AHA echo history_match (Claude genome, related) is not the same story; closest published is the 11-06 AHA rural heart-scan item, a different study. No overlap with today's science candidates; no cross-section assignment touches medicine.
